title: Soft Handoff Proxy and TTL Strategy for Stalled Tool Invocation Streams
creator: Riley Nakamura
description: Problem: When clients disconnect or exceed timeouts during long-running streaming generations that include tool (aka function) invocations or structured outputs, partial artifacts can remain allocated in runtime memory and cache layers. Existing cleanup is aggressive for fully-orphaned generations but fragile for in-flight tool calls and structured JSON outputs that need atomicity. This ticket proposes a Soft Handoff Proxy (SHP) and per-invocation TTL policy to reduce wasted GPU/kv-cache resources, allow safe resume in compatible clients, and provide a compatibility shim for older SDKs that don't support resume tokens.
proposal:
1) Introduce a lightweight Soft Handoff Proxy that takes over the socket/lease responsibilities for a short grace window after client disconnect. The SHP holds minimal metadata (lease token, last stable prefix, outstanding tool-call state) and a small bounded buffer for partial deltas.
2) Attach a per-invocation TTL and phased GC lifecycle (Grace -> SoftGC -> HardGC). Grace window allows resume, SoftGC drains cached KV prefixes and rewrites tool-call temp state to compact blobs, HardGC reclaims all allocations.
3) Emit a resume token when clients disconnect (if SDK supports). For older SDKs, enable compatibility-mode where SHP exposes a short-lived HTTP resume endpoint with polling semantics and a best-effort resume that maps to the nearest stable prefix.
4) Ensure structured-output boundaries and function call atomicity are respected: partial tool invocations move to a 'pending-tool' state and are either retried or forwarded to a safe fallback model when resumed.
design_decisions:
- Use a proxy component co-located with the runtime lane (same host) to avoid cross-host consistency costs.
- Keep SHP state bounded: limit buffered bytes and number of pending tool calls per invocation to control memory exposure.
- TTLs are configurable per-customer and per-tier; default: Grace=30s, SoftGC=5m, HardGC=1h.
- Compatibility shim default-off; opt-in per-application due to security surface.
- Structured output serial snapshots are taken at canonical punctuation boundaries to prevent emitting half-JSON when resuming.
implementation_notes:
Work split:
- Runtime: lease token plumbing, compacted partial snapshot API, tool-call pending-state marker (ENG runtime team)
- SHP service: lightweight in-process module exposing resume endpoint and managing TTL state
- SDK: resume-token generation and resume flow (JS/py first); opt-in polling shim for legacy SDKs
- Console/observability: new metrics (orphaned_invocations, resume_success_rate, softgc_count), dashboard panel and alerts

Important pragmatic choices:
- We'll store SHP metadata in the existing ephemeral metadata store (redis-like) with TTLs; larger snapshots go to S3-like cold storage on SoftGC.
- When a pending tool call cannot be safely resumed (external side-effect occurred), the SHP marks invocation as 'requires-compensation' and surfaces to ops.
- Implement an emergency hard-GC override accessible to SRE for noisy customers.

acceptance_criteria:
- Streaming invocations that include tool calls do not leak KV/cache allocations beyond HardGC for >95% of test cases.
- Resume token flow correctly restores state for compatible SDKs in 90th percentile of test workloads.
- Compatibility shim can resume ~60% of older SDK sessions without application changes.
- Observability: dashboard surfaces soft_gc_count and orphaned_invocations; Pager triggers only on HardGC rate spike.
- E2E test harness reproduces client disconnect at deterministic points (including mid-functioncall) and verifies eventual cleanup and resume behavior.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for SHP metadata lifecycle, boundary conditions for buffered sizes and TTL transitions.
- Integration tests: simulate sudden TCP disconnects, HTTP client timeouts, and slow consumer backpressure; assert no memory growth beyond configured limits.
- Fault injection: simulate external tool provider timeouts and ensure pending-tool state transitions to 'requires-compensation'.
- Compatibility regression: run legacy SDK matrix (JS 1.x, Python 0.9) against shim and measure resume success.
- Load test: synthetic workload with 5000 concurrent streams to measure SHP overhead and latency p99 delta.
rollout_plan:
- Feature gated via runtime flag and customer opt-in. Deploy SHP in canary lane with 10% traffic for 48 hours.
- Monitor metrics and run synthetic resume scenarios. If stable, enable for 50% then 100% on the runtime-1.20 release wave.
- Post-rollout: schedule customer-facing docs and SDK examples showing resume usage and compatibility-mode caveats.
